title: coord.py takes the time before it waits for the store's write lock, so a lease granted after a wait is short by that wait
goal: SP-rsmmwzr2 review G12 (ST-5iwikc3n): main and the server read time.time() before BEGIN IMMEDIATE, which may wait up to 30 s, so a lease granted after the wait expires early by its length and expiry decisions use a stale time. The time is read inside the transaction.

run:
import json,os,socket,subprocess as s,sys,tempfile,time
T='_tools/coord.py'
D=tempfile.mkdtemp()
E=dict(os.environ,KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(D,'c.db'))
def c(*a,t=30):
    p=s.run([sys.executable,T,*a],capture_output=True,text=True,env=E,timeout=t);return p.returncode,p.stdout,p.stderr
import sqlite3
c('list','--prefix','x')
db=sqlite3.connect(E['KB_COORD_STORE'],isolation_level=None);db.execute('BEGIN IMMEDIATE')
p=s.Popen([sys.executable,T,'claim','K6','--ttl','10','--holder','a'],stdout=s.PIPE,text=True,env=E)
time.sleep(2);db.execute('COMMIT');out=p.communicate(timeout=30)[0];t=time.time()
left=json.loads(out)['expires']-t
print('lease left after a 2 s lock wait:',round(left,2));sys.exit(0 if left>9.5 else 1)
